brief: Morgan Stanley (Andrew Sheets) frames four unresolved uncertainties. First, markets price 60% odds of a September rate hike, which the note attributes to competing readings of Fed Chair Warsh's Jackson Hole line that policy must be confident underlying inflation is moving to objective clearly and at sufficient speed. Because Morgan Stanley expects core inflation to decelerate in 2H 2026, it reads that framing as implying no action, and its economists forecast the Fed stays on hold, described as a close call. Second, the Treasury has not said whether doubling its buyback pace, per August 19th headlines, is forceful curve-flattening intervention or a $4bn adjustment against $40,000bn of debt. Third, AI outlays are forecast above $1.3 trillion for the six largest hyperscalers in 2027, 60% above the 2026 estimate, but which financing route across public and private markets absorbs it is unclear. Fourth, the bank rejects optimism on Strait of Hormuz normalization and, with Russian capacity disrupted, raises 4Q26 forecasts to $100/bbl Brent and EUR88/MWh TTF gas. Wide outcomes plus low expected volatility leave it positioned for higher macro volatility, underweight MBS, expecting record 2026 IG supply to widen spreads, preferring collateral-backed assets, and viewing energy equities as an oil hedge.
